question.problem:
Find the median of the random variable $X$ if the probability density function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<\frac{1}{2}, \\ \frac{3}{8{x}^{4}},\, & x\ge \frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The median of a random variable $X$ is the number $m$ such that

$$
P(X\le m)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le m) & ={\int }_{\frac{1}{2}}^{m}\frac{3}{8{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{8{x}^{3}}{|}_{\frac{1}{2}}^{m} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{8{m}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the median is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{1}{8{m}^{3}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{8{m}^{3}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ {m}^{3} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ m & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
